Explore illustrative model output from the 2026 irradiance export. Crop groups, temperature inputs, and harvest timing are scenario assumptions, not field observations.

Scenario assumptions — not field validation
SYNTHETIC INPUTS USED HERE — The Period Components export does not provide channel units/locations or air temperature. Channel groups below are unverified scenario assignments and irradiance is interpreted as W/m². Temperature-dependent outputs use supplemental typical-year air temperature, not measured temperatures from the irradiance year; crop-cycle fresh-mass equivalents also use an assumed 5% dry-matter fraction. Unrecorded irradiance timestamps are assumed to have zero light. Crop biomass values are uncalibrated model-derived scenario estimates, not validated yields: the growth equation, channel units, and dry-matter conversion are not calibrated for this site. Each bed cycle runs from transplant to GDD-001 harvest and the bed is replanted immediately. Estimated sowing dates are informational nursery-planning estimates only. Known limitation: the biomass equation gains more dry mass in cool air, opposite to measured lettuce growth, so cool-season values may be overstated. The final cycle may be incomplete. These are scenario outputs, not observed harvests or independent field validation. In this run the pipeline temperature input was TMY climatological air temperature from tmy_air_temperature.csv, UTC month/day/hour mapped to local standard-time hours (23.8°C), and the crop-cycle calculations use the same series. Detailed model state
Move the mouse over any graph to see all values at that exact time. Grey bands are night. Scroll over the graph to zoom; drag horizontally to move through time.
Each bed cycle runs from transplant (measured 0.90 g seedling, SITE-003) to the GDD-001 harvest date; the bed is replanted immediately. Known limitation: the growth model has no maturity slowdown, so each curve is steepest at harvest (CROP-004). Seasonal comparison not reliable: winter cycles last longer (GDD clock) and the growth model loses less to respiration in cool air and has no maturity slowdown, so cool-season harvests are overstated relative to summer (about 2x here vs about 25-40% in Brazilian field trials). Compare cycles within a season only. See CROP-004.
Modeled crop-cycle estimates (uncalibrated)

Fresh-mass equivalent = modeled field dry mass at harvest (including the transplanted seedling) divided by the assumed 5% dry-matter fraction. Each bed cycle runs from transplant to GDD harvest; estimated sowing dates are counted backwards with the same temperature series for nursery planning only. The per-plant conversion uses the configured 96 plants over 11.25 m². For context only, values are compared with the user-reported 100–300 g/plant range; those records are not currently available for calibration. These are not measured or validated harvests.

Seasonal comparison not reliable: winter cycles last longer (GDD clock) and the growth model loses less to respiration in cool air and has no maturity slowdown, so cool-season harvests are overstated relative to summer (about 2x here vs about 25-40% in Brazilian field trials). Compare cycles within a season only. See CROP-004.
